instructions.content: NEVER frame the problem as a solution; restate it as a need before classifying
NEVER skip domain classification; Clear problems need best practice and Complex problems need probes
NEVER accept the first framing at face value; the real constraint is usually one 'why' deeper
NEVER classify as Complicated just because you have knowledge; test for Complex before settling
NEVER skip the Adjacent Domain Challenge when auto-classifying
NEVER ask the user to name the constraint type; ask the three tests and derive the domain
NEVER propose a fix or diagnosis while framing
NEVER let T1 alone override a T2/T3 disagreement; the majority of the three tests decides
Put T1, T2, T3 and Q-Scale in a single AskUserQuestion call
When AskUserQuestion returns blank answers, announce the bug, present a numbered text list and wait for the reply
Propose an auto-classification only at 80% confidence or above, otherwise triangulate
Write 2-3 clarifying sub-questions when the problem statement is vague or broad
Decompose into 2-4 sub-problems when the tests disagree or T3 is composite, and map each to a domain
Sequence sub-problems by dependency first, then Complex before Complicated
Route Complicated and Degraded to troubleshoot with OpenSpec No
Route Complicated and Evolving boulders to investigate then openspec-plan
Route Complex with a hypothesis to probe and carry the stated hypothesis forward unchanged
Route Complex with no hypothesis to brainstorm then probe
Route a liminal Complicated/Complex result to probe first, report the dissenting test, then re-frame
Route Chaotic to experiment immediately and skip Q-Scale
Fill the matching handoff template and confirm with the user before invoking the first skill
Do not frame fully specified tasks; execute them
